intent.quote: Switch on the automatic approval if possible. Recover the quotes and perform the repin.
intent.readback: When plumb is sure enough of what you meant, it approves the record for you: JEV's confidence above 0.9 fast-tracks it; otherwise a model asks you a few questions through the question tool and JEV judges again, until the intent is clear. This covers intents, requirements and decisions alike, is learned from your own answers, is marked as the judge's everywhere, is undone when you say so, and runs only while you have switched it on.
will: Fast-track an intent, requirement or decision when JEV's confidence on it is above 0.9 and above its calibrated threshold, while you have the fast track on.
Otherwise hand it to the judge model, which asks you through the question tool, then have JEV judge again, until JEV or the model finds the intent clear.
Mark every judge approval with its judge and score, count it in the turn-end line, and undo it when you say so in conversation.
Calibrate JEV on your own answers with mixed evidence, and suspend the fast track when JEV's version changes.
Let only you switch the fast track: typed /plumb auto-approve on|off, or your answer to plumb's question.
wont: Approve any record from tests, links or a consistency check alone (settling by context stays removed).
Trial cards, read-back cards or buttons for calibration.
Let the agent, config.yaml or a sentence in prose switch the fast track.
Keep asking when the cascade cannot converge: that case goes to the debug workflow.
assumptions: 'Sonnet' in the owner's words is the configured judge model (P8's one judge_model setting), Sonnet by default.
The fast track stays off until the owner switches it on (DEC-016 holds); while off, every record goes the question route and its approval rests on the owner's answers.
The fast-track bar is the higher of 0.9 and JEV's calibrated no-false-accept threshold.
The cascade's round limit before the debug workflow is a setting, three rounds by default.
The confirmed P9 ('including intents') overrides DEC-073's 'never for intents'.

requirements.title: A record is approved by the judge cascade: JEV above 0.9 fast-tracks it, else the judge model asks through the question tool and JEV judges again
requirements.statement: A proposed intent, requirement or decision whose premise is the owner's verified words is approved without a question when the fast track is on and JEV scores it above 0.9 and above its calibrated threshold; the 0.9 floor is JEV's. Otherwise the judge model returns question-tool questions; after the owner answers, JEV judges again, and the record is approved when JEV clears the floor or the judge model says the intent is clear (its self-reported confidence is logged, never compared to a bar). With the fast track off, nothing is approved without a question round. An edit of a record the owner confirmed by their own answer, or one member of a set, is never fast-tracked: the edit goes to the judge model's questions, and a set is approved whole (P6). Tests, links or a consistency check never approve.

requirements.title: An older record's words are looked for in the owner's own past messages, and finding them approves nothing
requirements.statement: For a record whose words plumb never saw logged, the cascade looks for them in this project's past session transcripts, reading only messages the owner typed there; the judge model's question quotes the words found with their date, or says none were found and asks what the owner meant. A transcript match alone approves nothing, and an already approved record is skipped.

requirements.title: Only the owner switches the fast track, and a JEV version change suspends it
requirements.statement: The fast track works only while the owner's own switch event stands and calibration passes for the resolved JEV version; a change of JEV version beyond its normalized form suspends it. The owner switches it by typing /plumb auto-approve on|off as a whole message or by answering plumb's question; the agent, config.yaml or prose cannot.

requirements.title: Every judge approval is marked with its judge and counted; an entry under the cascade's bar is inert
requirements.statement: Each judge approval names its judge, score and model version wherever the record is listed, and is counted in the turn-end plumb line. An automatic approval entry that does not carry what the cascade requires (a JEV score above 0.9 and the calibrated threshold, or a judge model's clear verdict after a question round) is inert: the record counts as unapproved, and plumb validate reports the entry as a warning.

requirements.title: JEV is calibrated on the owner's own answers before it may fast-track
requirements.statement: Calibration pairs JEV's score logged at judgment time with the owner's own labels: question-tool answers confirming or correcting an interpretation, approvals by the owner's words, and reversals labelled 'no' as P4 says. A record kind passes only with mixed evidence: at least 20 owner labels and 5 'no' examples, at most half generated, no 'no' wrongly accepted. Each run logs threshold, false-accept rate and recall with model version and prompt digest. No trial card asks for labels.

decisions.question: What may approve a record without the owner's own words?
decisions.chosen: Only the judge cascade reading the owner's words: JEV above 0.9 and its calibrated threshold, else the judge model after the owner's question-tool answers, then JEV again; for intents, requirements and decisions alike whose premise is the owner's verified words; marked as the judge's, listed and reversible. Settling by context is removed.
alternatives: Keep settling by context alongside the judge.
JEV only; a judge model's verdict never approves.
No fast track: the owner answers a question for every record.

decisions.question: What switches the fast track on or off, given that the agent can edit .plumb/config.yaml?
decisions.chosen: Only the owner: /plumb auto-approve on|off typed as a whole message and seen by the prompt hook, or the owner's answer to plumb's question-tool question; each is logged as the owner's config event. config.yaml is a mirror; a yaml saying on without that event is off with a validate warning. The agent can never write the event.
alternatives: A deny rule on editing config.yaml.

decisions.question: When does a calibration pass for the fast track?
decisions.chosen: Mixed evidence per record kind: at least 20 of the owner's own labels and at least 5 'no' examples, at most half of which may be generated variations; JEV must wrongly accept none of them and accept at least half of the owner's approved records; the real/generated split is shown with the calibration.
alternatives: Only real 'no' examples, however few a project has.
Precision of at least 0.95 with any number of items.

decisions.question: How is an automatic approval entry that falls below the cascade's bar reported?
decisions.chosen: The entry is inert: the record counts as unapproved, so the merge holds it as it holds any unapproved record, and plumb validate reports the entry as a warning; errors stay for tampering and broken chains.
alternatives: An error that holds plumb's own merge boundary.
An error that only the owner's revocation clears.
